# Prep backlog is almost entirely producer-review flagged, starving the dispatcher's plan/intake fallback

## User story

As an operator, when the implement and audit budgets are exhausted, I want the dispatcher to have real plan/intake work to fall back to, so the local LLM slots are not left idle.

## Background

The host dispatch budget gates only `implement` and `audit`. `plan`, `intake` and `risk-effort` are deliberately uncapped, and since WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E / WL-0MWBT76WY00298AY a budget refusal is a continuable hold: the dispatcher records the refusal and steps on to the next ranked candidate, so a prep candidate behind a refused implement/audit can dispatch.

That fallback was supposed to keep the slots busy during the 2026-11-22/23 overnight run, but it had almost nothing to work with. Across the active roots, prep-stage supply at evaluation time (2026-11-23 10:15Z) was:

| Root | Prep-stage items (`idea`/`intake_complete`) | Admissible prep | Why not |
|---|---|---|---|
| ContextHub | 3 (`intake_complete`) | 0 | 2 x `needsProducerReview=true`; the third (WL-0MWRQYK3X007RQ1T) is a parent with 4 children and already has an outstanding `plan` dispatch marker at `intake_complete` |
| AI_Hell | 4 (`idea` + `intake_complete`) | 0 | all 4 `needsProducerReview=true` |
| SorraAgents | 1 (`intake_complete`) | 0 | `needsProducerReview=true` |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | 0 | 0 | no prep-stage items in the window |
| The Rising | 0 | 0 | no prep-stage items in the window |
| Game Curator | 0 | 0 | no prep-stage items in the window |

The leader therefore offered almost exclusively implement/audit candidates. Of 873 overnight refusals, 588 (67%) were `audit-budget-saturated`; the prep fallback could not fire because there was no admissible prep item to offer.

`plan_complete` items are implement candidates, not prep - a large `plan_complete` count does not help this fallback.

## Scope

1. Quantify prep-stage supply per active root: `idea` and `intake_complete` items, split by:
   - `needsProducerReview` (and the flag's provenance);
   - outstanding `plan`/`intake` dispatch marker at the current stage;
   - dependency/assignee/`startOn` hold;
   - attempt-budget or non-terminal-cooldown hold;
   - genuinely offerable.
2. For every producer-review-flagged prep item, establish provenance (which skill/phase set it: intake/plan question loop, audit reject, attempt-budget exhaustion, manual), age, and whether it has unresolved questions.
3. Write the root-cause statement for the empty prep bucket in the 2026-11-22/23 run, with counts.
4. Propose a remediation plan and create the follow-up work items:
   - clear stale `needsProducerReview` flags where there are no open questions;
   - batch producer interviews for items that genuinely need input;
   - change the skills so routine questions do not park items behind producer review;
   - seed new prep items where a root has none.
5. Verify the fix: for each active root, produce the `prep` bucket nominee in a live check-in (or an equivalent gate-classification read) and record it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A per-root table (ContextHub, AI_Hell, SorraAgents, Tableau-Card-Engine, The Rising, Game Curator) with the counts from Scope item 1, generated from `wl worklist --json` plus the gate predicates (not hand-sampled).
2. For every producer-review-flagged prep item: a row with `id`, title, flag provenance, flag age, and open-question status; grouped into "can clear now" vs "needs producer input".
3. A written root-cause statement for the empty prep bucket on 2026-11-22/23 with the evidence above (or corrected evidence if the investigation finds otherwise).
4. A remediation plan with concrete follow-up work items (each with an id, owner/queue and acceptance criteria) for stale-flag clearing, producer interview batching, skill changes and prep seeding.
5. Verification recorded: for each active root, the `prep` nominee from a live check-in (or the classification reason no nominee exists). Target: at least one admissible prep item on every active root, or a documented, justified exception.
6. Findings and follow-ups recorded on this work item; no dispatcher behaviour change in this item.

## Out of scope

- Changing the review-queue gate, the budget model, or the continuable-hold behaviour.
- Dispatching producer-review-flagged items without producer input.
- Implementing the remediation (separate items).

## Related

- WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E - Host-budget refusal early-returns from head scans, starving plan/intake behind an implement candidate (completed).
- WL-0MWBT76WY00298AY - Implement continuable hold predicate and fix head-scan early returns (completed).
- Overnight evidence: `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log`, `<root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*`, `<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.

## Impact

When the implement/audit budgets are full, the dispatcher has real plan/intake work to fall back to instead of leaving local LLM capacity idle.


## Plan

Decomposed into seven child features (test-first), each a deliverable slice; the measurement slice is built before any investigation depends on it.

| # | Child | Role | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test: prep-supply classification fixtures (WL-0MWTBJ5N1005BNXZ) | Pin the per-root prep-supply bucket semantics with fixtures before production code | — |
| 2 | Prep-supply report command (WL-0MWTBJ7G1004Y29B) | Read-only, repeatable per-root prep-supply read reusing the gate predicates | 1 |
| 3 | Per-root prep-supply table recorded (WL-0MWTBJ9AM003MLLL) | AC1 evidence: command output for all six roots, historical vs current | 2 |
| 4 | Producer-review provenance audit (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI) | AC2 evidence: provenance, age and open-question status per flagged item | 2 |
| 5 | Root-cause statement for empty prep bucket (WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE) | AC3: counted cause(s) for the 2026-11-22/23 window, correcting evidence if needed | 3, 4 |
| 6 | Remediation plan and follow-up items (WL-0MWTBJEI2008UGUR) | AC4: four follow-up items with ids, owners/queues and ACs | 3, 4 |
| 7 | Verification and findings handoff (WL-0MWTBJGBS0085DG1) | AC5 + AC6: per-root nominee/exception, no-behaviour-change evidence | 2, 5, 6 |

Working assumptions (recorded in the Appendix comment):

- The read reuses `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` in `packages/herdr` (no predicate moves between packages), matching the read-only attribution pattern of WL-0MVR8FKMU009XTED / WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR.
- The intake snapshot is a point-in-time reading; a live read on 2026-11-23 already differs materially, so the root cause is evidenced from the run window, not from the current state.
- AC5's "at least one admissible prep item on every active root" is verified per root at verification time, with the follow-up item that closes each remaining gap named — remediation itself stays out of this item (Out of scope).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-23T13:50Z — plan session `herdr-1795440935-1077826-4881`: created seven child features, wired ten dependency edges, ran the six review stages and the AC-coverage review (100% of ACs covered by children), estimated effort Medium / risk Medium. No dispatcher, gate or skill changes.

## Evidence

- **AC1 — per-root prep-supply table (recorded, reproducible):** comment WL-C0MWTQO4WW006YDIC; methodology, command, `--now` and raw-JSON hash in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Recorded prep-supply window (2026-11-23 10:15Z, WL-0MWTBJ9AM003MLLL)*. Child: WL-0MWTBJ9AM003MLLL.
- **AC2 — producer-review provenance audit (recorded, read-only):** comment WL-C0MWTTIOEN000M9LN — every flagged prep item's flag provenance, deciding evidence reference, flag age and open-question status, grouped *can clear now* (1) vs *needs producer input* (17); rule + recorded window in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Producer-review provenance* / *Recorded producer-review provenance audit*. Child: WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI.
- **AC3 - root-cause statement (recorded):** comment WL-C0MWTUHK5H004OL7E and section *Root cause* below; full evidence, commands and per-root tables in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` -> *Root cause: the 2026-11-22/23 empty prep bucket (WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE)*. Child: WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE.

## Root cause

The run's prep bucket was empty at the **offer** layer, not the **supply** layer. Counts are evidenced in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` -> *Root cause: the 2026-11-22/23 empty prep bucket (WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE)* and in comment WL-C0MWTUHK5H004OL7E on this item; the full statement with commands is on child WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE.

1. **No prep supply - refuted.** 397 prep-stage items existed at `2026-11-23T10:15:00Z` and 123 were offerable by re-derivation (ContextHub 27/10, AI_Hell 78/13, SorraAgents 238/83, Tableau-Card-Engine 11/1, tce-the-rising 42/15, games_curator 1/1).
2. **The offer window was fully gated.** On the two roots that logged a gate classification every tick, 100% of the scanned candidate slots were gated (ContextHub 4,165/4,165: review-queue-hold 1,782 + audit-fresh 1,259 + producer-review 944 + code-freeze 88 + dispatched-marker 86 + 6 other; games_curator 768/768: producer-review 576 + audit-fresh 192). The dominant hold was the completed/in_review queue, not prep.
3. **The drain bucket was budget-capped.** 588 of 873 refusal decisions (67%) were `audit-budget-saturated`, 738 of them (84.5%) with both LLM slots free; the audit bucket that could drain the review queue was refused machine-wide.
4. **Producer review is real but minority.** 18 of 416 prep items were flagged (4.3%); 17 carry an unanswered producer question and the one clearable row is independently held by six unmet dependencies, so clearing could not dispatch it. That cannot explain an empty bucket while 123 prep items were offerable.
5. **Corrected intake evidence.** (a) The 873/588 figures come from `<root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*` `kind=decision, operation=no-dispatch` entries, not from `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` (1,029 reserve/confirm/sweep entries, zero refusals); (b) they are the recorded reading at `2026-11-23T10:12Z` and are no longer reproducible - the rolling 500-line logs have rotated, and re-running the intake command returns 0; (c) the "3/4/1/0/0/0 prep, 0 admissible" snapshot was a windowed reading that under-counted supply by ~10x on the large roots; (d) "almost entirely producer-review flagged" applies to the bounded scan window share (22.7% ContextHub / 75% games_curator), not to the 4.3% it represents of the prep backlog.

**Time dependence.** The window figures are historical and cannot be replayed (`wl` has no item-state history; `--now` freezes only time-derived gates). The current state differs: at `2026-11-23T22:32Z` the same read is 413 prep items / 128 offerable / 16 producer-review-held (the recorded 10:15Z read was 416 / 123 / 18; two ContextHub `ruff DTZ007` flags were cleared externally at `22:00Z` and one startOn matured). SorraAgents alone holds 238 prep items at the window clock (93 open, 145 blocked) versus the 1 in the intake snapshot.

**Open questions.** (i) A check-in records only `workItemId`, which mirrors `offers[0]` under v2; the per-entry `offers` payload is not persisted, so a prep nominee behind a non-prep head is not excluded by this evidence. (ii) There is no durable refusal log: the coordinator logs rotate within hours, so an overnight post-mortem cannot be re-derived - a durable refusal log (or longer retention) is a follow-up.


## Scope item 4 answer: remediation plan and follow-up items (WL-0MWTBJEI2008UGUR)

Four follow-up items, one per bucket, each linked back to this item and carrying the evidence rows. Planning only: no flag cleared, no skill edited, no dispatcher behaviour change.

| Bucket | Follow-up | Owner/queue | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4a stale-flag clearing | WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV | dispatcher maintainer / operator | Clears only the **1** `can-clear-now` row (`AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P`, dependency-held); the 17 `needs-producer-input` rows stay flagged. |
| 4b producer interview batching | WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER | producer | Batches the **17** `needs-producer-input` rows into one interview; each flag clears only when its question is answered. |
| 4c skill changes | WL-0MWTVPL1A005KB4D | skill maintenance (SorraAgents `skill/`) | **16 of 18** flagged rows are `question-loop`; routine questions must record an assumption instead of setting the hold. |
| 4d prep seeding | WL-0MWTVPM0D009FMG3 | dispatcher maintainer / operator | Guard: seed only a root with zero offerable prep; all six roots had >=1 offerable at 10:15Z (123/416), so this is a no-op unless a live read finds an empty root. |

**Dependency edges:** 4a and 4b depend on the provenance audit's `can-clear-now` / `needs-producer-input` groupings (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI); 4c and 4d have no blocking prerequisite. **Duplicate checks** are recorded on each follow-up (search terms + results; no scope duplicated).

# Allow 2x implement/audit budget while panes wait for a model to be re-enabled

## User story

As an operator, when an implement or audit pane is stuck waiting for a model/provider to be re-enabled, I want the dispatcher to keep the local LLM slots earning by admitting extra implement/audit work, up to double the configured budget, instead of idling at the normal cap.

## Background

`model-cooldowns.json` is the machine-wide signal that a pane is blocked on a throttled provider (`cooldownUntil > now`); the stalled-work scan already treats an active entry as "never wake early" and a due entry as a wake trigger (WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7). The host-budget dispatcher nevertheless counts those panes as live and refuses new work at the configured cap (`maxImplement`, `maxAudit`), even though the blocked panes cannot use the model.

The 2026-11-22/23 overnight run showed the cost: 14 agent sessions open (5 implement, 5+ audit, 1 intake), 175 provider-exhaustion turns across 42 sessions, and several sessions 11-17 h old. The fleet idled at the configured caps while panes waited for the provider to come back.

## Detection

A pane is **model-blocked** when it has an active machine-wide model-cooldown entry (matched by `paneId` or `sessionId`) whose kind is `implement` or `audit` - kind from the entry when present, otherwise from the pane label. This is the canonical "waiting on a model to be re-enabled" signal.

If the implementation also consumes a proxy model-availability signal (model disabled/loading/switching), it must be documented and tested. Absent, unreadable or corrupt signals must **not** grant relief (fail closed).

## Relief rule

- While at least one model-blocked pane of a capped kind exists, that kind's admission cap is `min(2 x configured cap, hard ceiling)`, where the hard ceiling is **2x the configured cap** and cannot be raised by settings or env.
- The total live count (including the blocked panes) must not exceed the effective cap.
- Relief is **per kind**: a blocked implement raises only the implement cap; a blocked audit raises only the audit cap.
- Plan/intake/risk-effort remain uncapped and are not affected.
- Relief ends immediately when the last matching cooldown expires or is cleared: the cap returns to the configured value on the next admission read, with no restart and no stuck double cap.
- Relief only raises the host-budget cap; every other gate (free slots, prefill pacing, CPU, review-queue depth, producer review, attempt budget, code-freeze, audit freshness) is unchanged.

## Audit-arm dependency (must not be faked)

The proxy audit lease remains authoritative (`/llama/local/audit/availability`, `cap`, atomic `/llama/local/audit/lease`). herdr must never invent a second lease. If the proxy still grants `cap: 1`, an audit relief dispatch must still refuse `audit-budget-saturated`. The item must land one of:

- a coordinated proxy contract that grants a relief audit cap while an audit is model-blocked; or
- an explicit, documented scoping of the audit arm to the legacy local-budget mode (`HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1`) with evidence, until the proxy supports relief.

The implement arm must not be blocked on the audit-arm dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A documented, unit-tested model-blocked predicate: an active entry for an implement/audit pane -> blocked; expired/absent -> not blocked; corrupt/unreadable signal -> not blocked (fail closed); unknown kind -> not blocked; kind resolved from the pane label when the entry's kind is `null`.
2. `admitHostDispatch` computes `effectiveCap(kind) = min(configuredCap x 2, 2 x configuredCap)` while a model-blocked pane of that kind exists; otherwise `configuredCap`. Per-kind independence is pinned (blocked implement does not raise audit and vice versa).
3. The effective cap is a **total live** cap including the blocked panes; admission refuses above it with the normal budget token. No path can admit beyond the effective cap.
4. A clock-advance test proves relief ends when `cooldownUntil` passes and the cap reverts without a restart.
5. A corrupt/unreadable `model-cooldowns.json` (reader returns `null`) yields the normal cap, with decision evidence naming the unreadable signal.
6. Audit arm: a test proves herdr never invents a lease; with proxy `cap: 1` an audit relief dispatch remains `audit-budget-saturated`; the proxy contract change (or legacy-mode scoping) is recorded as a dependency with its own work item if required.
7. Both dispatcher paths (coordination leader `dispatchFromCoordination` and direct `dispatchDowntimeWork`) produce the same effective cap; a pin asserts there is no path that bypasses `admitHostDispatch`.
8. Table-driven proof that relief never relaxes any other gate (free slots, prefill cap/ETA, CPU, review-queue hold, producer review, attempt budget, code-freeze, audit freshness).
9. Decision-log evidence `budgetRelief: { kind, baseCap, effectiveCap, blockedPaneIds, reason, until }` is recorded on an admission with relief and on a refusal above the effective cap; a `budget-relief` header/decision token is added to the vocabulary; the worklist counter shows `n/effectiveCap`.
10. Kill switch `downtimeBudgetReliefEnabled` (default `true`) restores the configured cap when off; the multiplier is fixed at 2 and cannot be raised by settings or env.
11. Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `CONFIG.md`, and the model-cooldown contract header (`packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`) notes the new consumer.
12. Changed-scope and full test suites green before `in_review`.

## Out of scope

- Raising the proxy's slot count or `max_audits` beyond the relief rule; the proxy remains the authority for audit leases.
- Auto-resuming or aborting model-blocked panes (that is the stalled-work wake path).
- Exceeding 2x under any circumstances.

## Related

- WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7 - bounded model-cooldown wake (machine-wide signal + stalled-work integration).
- WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI / WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD - host dispatch budget and proxy-derived audit admission.
- WL-0MWDDHVF2004PTYX - audit-budget refusal precedence and evidence.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/model-cooldowns.json` - the machine-wide signal.

## Impact

When a dispatched implement or audit is parked waiting for its model to come back, herdr can keep otherwise-idle local LLM slots earning by admitting additional implement/audit work up to double the normal cap, instead of idling at the configured budget.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-23)

Decomposition: 11 children in four vertical-slice phases, each cutting through module + tests + wiring + observability + docs; every phase is preceded by its test item (test-first ordering is enforced with dependency edges).

| Phase | Children | Slice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — predicate and cap contract | Test: model-blocked predicate and relief cap (WL-0MWTASN6H0005KED) -> Implement: host-budget-relief predicate and cap (WL-0MWTASWOE0033YEH) | new pure module, unit suite, contract-of-record header |
| 2 — admission and surfaces | Test: relief admission across both dispatcher paths (WL-0MWTASOSV0004O6J) -> Implement: relief in admission and dispatcher (WL-0MWTASY9100813PD) -> Implement: relief evidence and budget counters (WL-0MWTASZNA008AQOK) | `admitHostDispatch` + both dispatcher paths + decision log + worklist header + skip line + interactive threshold |
| 3 — operator control and audit arm | Implement: downtimeBudgetReliefEnabled kill switch (WL-0MWTAT1O300673UQ), Test: audit lease authority under relief (WL-0MWTASQDU002HDYR) -> Implement: audit-arm relief scoping (WL-0MWTAT3090003CA6) | settings kill switch, lease-authority pin, legacy-mode scoping |
| 4 — regression, docs, verification | Test: relief relaxes no other gate (WL-0MWTASS0T0037XP6), Docs: budget relief contract (WL-0MWTAT4BP0055B8T) -> Verify: acceptance criteria and green suites (WL-0MWTAT65H009VPAQ) | non-relaxation matrix, four docs, AC evidence + green suites |

Decisions taken while planning (each is a documented assumption, reversible):

- **Fixed multiplier.** Relief is exactly 2x and lives as a module constant in `host-budget-relief.ts`; no setting, no `budget.json` key and no env var can raise it (parent AC10). `HOST_BUDGET_MAX = 32` continues to bound only the *configured* cap.
- **Audit arm (parent AC6, option 2).** Audit relief is scoped to the legacy local-budget mode (`HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1`) with evidence, because the proxy lease is authoritative and herdr must never invent a second lease. No cross-repo work item is created; the proxy contract change is recorded as a documented dependency inside the audit-arm children. The implement arm is not blocked by it.
- **Interactive threshold.** The hand-fired over-quota dialog uses the same effective cap as admission, so the header (`5/10`) and the prompt cannot disagree. Human override above the effective cap is unchanged.
- **Signal.** `~/.herdr/downtime/model-cooldowns.json` is the only relief signal; no proxy model-availability (disabled/loading/switching) signal is consumed or inferred.
- **Fail direction.** An unreadable/corrupt cooldown read grants no relief (fail closed) and records evidence naming the unreadable signal — the opposite of the reader's own "assume active" convention, deliberately, so a corrupt file cannot inflate the host budget.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which of the two parent AC6 options should the audit arm land — a coordinated proxy contract that grants a relief audit cap, or scoping audit relief to the legacy local-budget mode?" — Answer (plan, from the item's own AC6 and the shipped admission contract): **legacy-mode scoping**, with the proxy lease remaining authoritative. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` (two-step availability pre-check + atomic lease), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §proxy-derived audit admission. **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, producer may override):** if the producer prefers the coordinated proxy contract, the audit-arm children change and a proxy-repo item is required; the implement arm is unaffected.
- Q: "Should the fixed 2x multiplier be reachable from settings/env so an operator can tune it?" — Answer (plan, from parent AC10): no. Evidence: AC10 pins "the multiplier is fixed at 2 and cannot be raised by settings or env".
- Q: "Does relief need to consume a proxy model-availability signal (disabled/loading/switching)?" — Answer (plan, from the parent Detection section): no; the machine-wide cooldown file is the canonical signal, and any future proxy signal needs its own documented, tested change. Evidence: `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts` contract header, `~/.herdr/downtime/model-cooldowns.json` (3 active entries observed at planning time: audit, intake, implement).
- Q: "Should relief relax the interactive over-quota dialog threshold?" — Answer (plan): yes, to the same effective cap, so the counter and the prompt agree; the human-override path above the effective cap is unaffected. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts`.
- Research: duplicate-work detection — searched `wl` for "budget relief", "admitHostDispatch", "model-cooldown", "host dispatch budget", "maxImplement", "double budget", "2x budget", "model blocked". No open duplicate exists; the nearest completed predecessors are WL-0MWF34932000SNTX (generic admission), WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD (admission choke point) and WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7 (bounded cooldown wake). Result: no overlap requiring closure or rewrite.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-23 — plan skill: decomposed into 11 children (4 phases), wired 13 dependency edges (test before implementation in every phase), recorded the five planning decisions above, and recorded the Appendix. Pre-check: `plan-if-needed` returned `plan` (effort Large, risk High); approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (Extra Large + High risk not met). AC coverage review: 100% covered, `proceed`.

## Parent

WL-0MWTAD9NV000IVK5 — Allow 2x implement/audit budget while panes wait for a model to be re-enabled. Covers parent AC1, AC4 (unit level) and AC5 (unit level).

**Test-first item: no production code here.** This suite pins the relief predicate and the effective-cap arithmetic and must fail until the sibling implement item (`host-budget-relief.ts`) lands.

## Scope

One focused, pure unit suite for the new relief module: a table-driven "model-blocked pane" predicate and the effective-cap arithmetic, driven by an injected clock and in-memory cooldown/pane fixtures (no file I/O, no `Date.now()`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new suite `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-relief.test.ts` covers the body of AC1: an active entry (`cooldownUntil > now`) for an `implement` or `audit` pane is blocked; an expired entry is not blocked; an absent signal (`[]`) is not blocked; an unreadable/corrupt signal (`null`) is not blocked (fail closed); an unknown or absent kind is not blocked; an entry whose `kind` is `null` is resolved from the pane label.
- The predicate matches an entry to a pane by `paneId` first, then by `sessionId`, and a session-only entry (no `paneId`) matches only when the pane's session id is known.
- Per-kind independence is pinned: a blocked implement produces a blocked set for `implement` only (and an empty set for `audit`), and vice versa.
- The effective cap is pinned as `min(baseCap * 2, hardCeiling)` where the hard ceiling equals `2 * baseCap`, i.e. relief is exactly 2x while a model-blocked pane of that kind exists, and the configured cap otherwise.
- A table asserts the multiplier is a fixed module constant (`2`) and cannot be raised by settings or an environment variable (an env var and a settings-shaped object are supplied and the result is unchanged).
- A clock-advance table proves relief ends when `cooldownUntil` passes, with no restart and no stuck double cap (same in-memory state, advanced clock).
- A base cap of `0` (tier disabled) stays `0` under relief: relief never revives a disabled tier.
- The suite is runnable through the test skill (`/skill:test`) changed scope and fails before the implementation lands.

- A test asserts relief consults NO proxy model-availability signal: the machine-wide `model-cooldowns.json` is the only relief signal, and no availability seam is read by the predicate.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-relief.test.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.fixtures.ts` (reuse existing fixture helpers where they fit)

## Notes

- Do not invoke `pytest`/`vitest`/`npm test` directly — route every run through `/skill:test`.
- Signal shape is the machine-wide model-cooldown entry (`packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`): `paneId`, `sessionId`, `itemId`, `kind`, `cooldownUntil`.

## Parent

WL-0MWTAD9NV000IVK5 — Allow 2x implement/audit budget while panes wait for a model to be re-enabled. Covers parent AC2, AC3 and AC7.

Depends on the admission-test item; implement until that suite is green with no regression in the existing budget suites.

## Scope

Thread the model-blocked signal into the ONE admission read and both dispatcher paths, with a single read per tick and no new refusal token.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `admitHostDispatch` computes the effective cap through the shared resolver (`resolveEffectiveHostBudgetCap`) — the single computation AC2 asks for — and compares the total live count (blocked panes included) against it, refusing with the kind's existing `host-budget-<kind>` token.
- An active-cooldown read happens once per dispatch tick/attempt through `machine-coordination.ts` (a new `readActiveModelCooldowns()` wrapper over `readModelCooldowns(dir, now)`), never once per candidate, and the result is threaded to admission through the dispatcher deps seam.
- The pane projection carries a session id (derived with `sessionIdFromSessionPath`) so a session-only cooldown entry matches its pane; a failed pane read degrades to no relief (fail closed) rather than to a partial match.
- Both dispatcher paths (`dispatchFromCoordination` and `dispatchDowntimeWork`) reach admission through the same seam and receive the same blocked projection, so their caps are identical by construction.
- Every other budget behaviour is untouched: ledger counting, reservation/confirm/release, the corrupt-ledger fail-closed arm, `no-coordination-dir` admission, `max = 0` refusal and uncapped-kind short circuit behave exactly as before when no cooldown is active.
- `host-budget-relief.test.ts`, `host-dispatch-budget*.test.ts` and the coordination/dispatch-claims suites are green.
- The changed-scope suite is green.

- Delivered parent criterion (WL-0MWTAD9NV000IVK5): `admitHostDispatch` computes `effectiveCap(kind) = min(configuredCap x 2, 2 x configuredCap)` while a model-blocked pane of that kind exists; otherwise `configuredCap`. Per-kind independence is pinned (blocked implement does not raise audit and vice versa).

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD (prep backlog starves the dispatcher's plan/intake fallback).

Test-first slice: pin the **per-root prep-supply classifier** bucket semantics with fixture-driven tests *before* any production code exists, so the measurement the rest of this item depends on cannot silently drift.

## Context

`classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts`) already returns a stable gate token for every refusal (`producer-review`, `assignee-hold`, `startOnNotReached`, `not-dispatchable`, `effort-cap`, …) — see WL-0MVR8FKMU009XTED. The prep-supply report adds only the dispatcher-side gates the classifier does not cover: an outstanding `plan`/`intake` dispatch marker at the current stage, attempt-budget exhaustion, and non-terminal cooldown. It must never re-implement the classifier's predicates.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new fixture-driven test module builds per-root windows from inline JSON (no live DB, no `wl` subprocess) and asserts the bucket for every case: offerable prep, `needsProducerReview=true`, outstanding dispatch marker at the current stage, non-empty `assignee`, future `startOn`, unmet dependency, attempt-budget exhaustion, non-terminal cooldown.
- Tests pin the bucket **precedence order** (producer-review → dispatch marker → hold → attempt/cooldown → offerable) with at least one fixture where several causes apply simultaneously, asserting the single reported primary cause.
- A negative case asserts a `plan_complete` item is never counted as prep supply, and that `completed`/`in_review`/`deleted` items never appear in any prep bucket.
- Tests assert **read-only** behaviour: no `wl` write is invoked, and the classified dispatch decisions are identical with and without the report module loaded.
- Tests assert the bucket names match the documented table in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (one source of truth; drift fails the suite).
- Changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply.test.ts` — new fixture-driven tests (does not exist yet)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (asserted, never modified)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `DowntimeItemInfo` fixture shape
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — canonical gate/bucket vocabulary

## Constraints

- No sleeps, no network, no live worklog; fixtures only.
- Must not modify gate behaviour — a failing assertion here is a finding for the parent item, not a licence to change predicates.

## Impact

The operator can rely on the prep-supply measurement: every prep item's bucket and single primary cause is pinned by fixtures, so a drift in the classifier-to-bucket mapping fails the suite instead of quietly changing the reported counts.
data.title: Test: prep-supply classification fixtures

data.description:
## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Give the operator a **repeatable, read-only** per-root answer to "how much prep work could the dispatcher actually offer, and why not?" instead of a hand-classified sample.

## Context

The 2026-11-22/23 overnight run burned 873 refusals (588 `audit-budget-saturated`) with an empty prep bucket, and diagnosing it required classifying items by hand. `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` already attributes each refusal to a stable gate token; what is missing is a per-root, prep-tier-specific read that also applies the worker-side gates (dispatch marker, attempt budget, cooldown) and reports the genuinely offerable set.

Reuse, do not fork: `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`), `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`, the marker/hold predicates in `downtime-worker.selection.ts`, and the read-only attribution pattern established by WL-0MVR8FKMU009XTED / WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR.

## Acceptance criteria

- A read-only command/diagnostic emits **per-root JSON plus a human table** with counts per bucket: `offerable`, `producer-review`, `dispatch-marker`, `assignee-hold`, `dependency`, `startOn`, `attempt-budget`, `cooldown`, `other-gated` — and lists the offerable item ids.
- Inputs come from `wl worklist --json` where it already covers the item, plus a full per-root item read where the worklist has no prep subset; the gap and the fallback are documented in the command help and in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- The command accepts an explicit repeatable `--root <path>` (or reads the active-root set from config when omitted) and a `--now <iso>` frozen clock, so a past window can be replayed deterministically.
- Strictly read-only: no `wl` write, no marker/flag/assignee mutation. A regression test asserts the dispatcher's dispatched-item set is byte-identical with and without the report module.
- Output is stable and diffable — sorted by root, then bucket, then item id — so two runs can be compared in review.
- Bucket definitions and usage are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, cross-referenced from `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts` — new report module (does not exist yet)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (reused)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — marker/hold predicates (reused)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — item shape and gate-token types
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — only if a prep subset is added to `wl worklist --json`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — bucket table and usage

## Constraints

- No change to any dispatch decision, gate, cap or budget (parent AC6 / Out of scope).
- Do not move `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` into another package: reuse it in place, from herdr.


## Impact

When the implement and audit budgets are full, an operator can now see in one read-only command — per root and replayable at a past instant — how much plan/intake work the dispatcher could actually offer and the primary cause blocking everything else, instead of classifying items by hand.

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Produce the **per-root prep-supply table** (parent AC1) as command output — not a hand sample — and reconcile it against the intake snapshot.

## Context

The intake table was assembled by hand at 2026-11-23 10:15Z. A live read on 2026-11-23 13:4xZ already disagrees materially (e.g. SorraAgents now shows ~93 open prep-stage items and AI_Hell ~22), so the "empty prep bucket" is a **point-in-time** finding that must be evidenced from the run window, not from today's state.

## Acceptance criteria

- A per-root table for ContextHub, AI_Hell, SorraAgents, Tableau-Card-Engine, The Rising and Game Curator is generated from `wl worklist --json` plus the gate predicates (not hand-sampled) — produced by running the prep-supply report across all six roots (paths: `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`, `SorraAgents`, `Tableau-Card-Engine`, `tce-the-rising`, `games_curator`), with the exact command line, `--now` timestamp and raw JSON reference recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Bucket counts reconcile: the sum of buckets equals the count of prep-stage items in the window for every root, asserted by the command itself (no silent drops).
- The table records the historical-vs-current divergence explicitly: the 10:15Z snapshot from the description alongside the live read, with the re-derived window from the evidence logs wherever they disagree.
- Any row that had to be corrected carries an inline note saying why (a hand-edited count is not acceptable as the primary source — the primary source is command output).
- The table is reproducible: re-running the recorded command at the recorded `--now` yields the same table (modulo live data drift, which the timestamp pins).
- Recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` as a comment and linked from its description.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — where the recorded table/methodology belongs
- `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` — refusal evidence for the same window

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. For every producer-review-flagged prep item, establish **where the flag came from, how long it has been set, and whether anything is actually waiting on the producer** — split into "can clear now" vs "needs producer input" (parent AC2).

## Context

The flag is the dispatcher's only persistent hold (`needsProducerReview === true` → `producer-review` gate). It can be set by the `intake`/`plan`/`interview` question loops, by an audit rejection, by attempt-budget exhaustion, or by hand. Nothing records provenance, so a stale flag is indistinguishable from a live question — which is what starved the fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written **provenance rule** covering each flag source (intake/plan/interview question loop, audit reject, attempt-budget exhaustion, manual), naming the exact evidence fields it keys on (`auditResult`, last comment author/text, dispatch marker, timestamps) and its fail-closed behaviour when the evidence is ambiguous.
- For every producer-review-flagged prep item a row with `id`, title, flag provenance, flag age and open-question status; grouped into "can clear now" vs "needs producer input", recorded for every prep item with `needsProducerReview=true` on each active root with its deciding evidence reference (comment id / audit id / marker) and the flag age measured from that evidence's timestamp.
- Rows are grouped into **"can clear now"** (no open questions) and **"needs producer input"** (an unanswered question is recorded), with group counts per root and in total.
- Sanity check: the rule is applied to at least three items with documented history and its assignment matches that history (mismatch is recorded as an open question, not silently overridden).
- The audit is **read-only**: no flag is cleared, no item is reassigned (clearing is a separate follow-up).
- Findings recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes if a provenance helper or rule test is added.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `producer-review` gate token (the predicate being explained)
- `docs/dev/rca-wrongful-needsproducerreview-removal.md` — history of the flag and its lifecycle
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — flag semantics and hold rules
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/{intake,plan,interview,audit,implement}/SKILL.md` — the call sites that set the flag

## Dependencies

Depends on the prep-supply report command (needs the classified item set as input).

## Impact

An operator can now see, for every producer-review-flagged prep item, what put the flag there, how stale it is and whether a real producer question is waiting — so stale flags can be cleared from evidence instead of guesswork.

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Write the **root-cause statement** for the empty prep bucket in the 2026-11-22/23 run — or correct the intake evidence if the measurement disagrees (parent AC3).

## Context

The intake hypothesis is: prep supply existed but was almost entirely `needsProducerReview`-held, so the leader had nothing to offer behind a refused implement/audit head. A live read on 2026-11-23 already contradicts the "no supply" reading for several roots, so the statement must separate *supply*, *gating*, and *time dependence* explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written root-cause statement for the empty prep bucket on 2026-11-22/23 with the evidence above (or corrected evidence if the investigation finds otherwise): the statement names the cause(s) with counts for the window and explicitly distinguishes **no prep supply** from **prep supply held by gates**, per root.
- Every number is traceable to evidence with the command used: `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` refusal counts (873 refusals / 588 = 67% `audit-budget-saturated`), the per-root coordination/dispatch logs, and the prep-supply table.
- Where re-derivation disagrees with the intake table, the statement says so explicitly ("corrected evidence: was X, now Y, because Z") rather than silently rewriting it.
- The statement separates the historical window from the current state and labels which findings are time-dependent (e.g. "SorraAgents has ~93 open prep items today, 1 at 10:15Z").
- Every claim is traceable to a row/count in the prep-supply or provenance findings; unsupported claims are removed or marked OPEN QUESTION.
- Recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` as the "Root cause" section.

- `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` (+ `.1` rotation) — refusal evidence
- `<root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*` — per-root check-in/offer evidence
- `<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — per-root dispatch history

## Impact

An operator reading the overnight logs can now see that the prep bucket was empty because the scanned candidate window was fully gated - not because there was no prep work - and knows which evidence must be retained to prove it next time.

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Turn the findings into a **remediation plan with concrete follow-up work items** (parent AC4) — planning only: no flags are cleared, no skill is edited and no dispatcher behaviour changes in that parent item.

## Acceptance criteria

- A remediation plan with concrete follow-up work items (each with an id, owner/queue and acceptance criteria) for stale-flag clearing, producer interview batching, skill changes and prep seeding — four items, each linked back to `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` with the evidence rows that justify it.
  - (a) clear stale `needsProducerReview` flags where no open question exists;
  - (b) batch producer interviews for the items that genuinely need producer input;
  - (c) change the `intake`/`plan`/`interview` skills so routine questions do not park items behind producer review;
  - (d) seed new prep items on roots that have none.
- Each follow-up names the evidence rows (from the prep-supply table / provenance audit / root-cause statement) that justify it, and links back to `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Dependency edges are wired: stale-flag clearing depends on the provenance audit's "can clear now" grouping; interview batching depends on the "needs producer input" grouping; the skill-change and prep-seeding items have no blocking prerequisite.
- Duplicate check recorded: each proposed follow-up is checked against existing open/completed work with `wl search`/`wl list` and the search terms plus results are noted (no new item duplicating existing scope).
- The four buckets above are covered: stale-flag clearing, producer interview batching, skill changes, prep seeding — one item each, no bucket merged or dropped.
- Remediation stays **planned only** in this item: no flag cleared, no skill file edited, and no dispatcher behaviour change (verified by an unchanged dispatched-item set).
- Scope item 4 of `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` is answered in its description with the follow-up ids and a one-line rationale for each.

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/interview/SKILL.md` — the producer-review handoff text the skill-change follow-up will target (read, not edited)

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Record the **verification** (parent AC5) and the findings handoff (parent AC6): per root, the live `prep` nominee or the classification reason none exists, mapped to the follow-up item that would close each gap.

## Context

Parent AC5 asks for "at least one admissible prep item on every active root, or a documented, justified exception". Because remediation is explicitly out of the parent's scope, this verification records the **state at verification time** plus, for each root with no nominee, the follow-up item that would create one — the "≥1 per root" target becomes the exit criterion tracked on those follow-ups.

## Acceptance criteria

- Verification recorded: for each active root, the `prep` nominee from a live check-in (or the classification reason no nominee exists), produced by the prep-supply report / gate-classification read with the read timestamp (not hand-picked). Target: at least one admissible prep item on every active root, or a documented, justified exception — evaluated root by root with the outcome stated explicitly.
- Each root with no nominee is mapped to the specific follow-up item from the remediation plan that would close it; roots that already have an admissible prep item are marked "none needed".
- The per-root target ("≥1 admissible prep item, or a documented, justified exception") is evaluated root by root and the outcome stated explicitly.
- Findings and follow-ups are recorded on this work item, and there is no dispatcher behaviour change in this item: the dispatched-item set and offer computation are byte-identical before and after.
- A pointer table shows where each of parent AC1–AC6 is evidenced, and cites the regression test proving the byte-identical dispatched-item set (no gate, cap or budget code changed).
- Changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts` — the read used for the nominees
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — classification reasons quoted per root

## Dependencies

## Impact

## Goal

Clear the `needsProducerReview` flag on the prep item(s) that the producer-review provenance audit proves clearable, so a stale flag stops hiding otherwise-dispatchable prep work from the dispatcher's plan/intake fallback.

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD (Scope item 4a). Discovered-from: WL-0MWTBJEI2008UGUR.

## Owner / queue

- **Owner:** dispatcher maintainer / operator (agent-executable run; producer sign-off recorded before clearing).

# Driven implement child sessions abort on a transient 'Provider finish_reason: error'

**Headline:** A driven `implement.py` child session dies when the local model proxy answers mid-stream with `finish_reason: "error"`, and the drive loop hard-stops because it cannot tell that transient provider hiccup from a genuine defect — so one flaky reply costs the operator a manual re-run of the whole epic.

## Problem statement

When `implement.py drive` spawns a child session for an epic's work item, that child can exit non-zero with `Provider finish_reason: error` after the local model proxy (at `http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1`) returns `finish_reason: "error"` mid-stream. `classify_spawn_failure` does not recognise this reason, so it returns `unknown`, the `--infra-retry-limit` budget never engages, and the drive chain abandons the child. During the 2026-11-23/24 run of WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD this forced **25+ manual `implement.py drive` invocations over ~5.3 h**; one child needed 20 consecutive failed spawns before a session survived.

## Users

- **Primary:** the operator/agent supervising a driven epic. Story: *As an operator running `implement.py drive` on a 7-child epic, I want a single transient provider reply to be retried inside the drive budget, so I am not babysitting the chain with 25 manual re-runs.*
- **Secondary:** the downtime dispatcher, which runs the same drive path unattended overnight. Story: *As the overnight dispatcher, I want a flaky local-model window to consume bounded retries rather than abandon the epic, so progress resumes without any human present.*
- **Tertiary:** a future maintainer. Story: *As a maintainer, I want the diagnosis of why the child's recovery extension did not save it recorded, so I do not "fix" this at the wrong layer.*

## Existing state

- `classify_spawn_failure` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) classifies only two fragments as `infrastructure` via `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS`: `No models match pattern` and `No API key found for`. Every other reason — including `Provider finish_reason: error` — is `unknown`, which is fail-safe but hard-stops the chain.
- The drive loop (`phase_drive`) already has the right machinery: an `infrastructure` classification is retried on the shared `--infra-retry-limit` budget with exponential backoff, the same child in the same worktree, plus a durable child comment.
- **Diagnosis already evidenced:** driven children are spawned as `pi -p "/skill:implement <id>" --approve --no-extensions` (`_default_session_spawner`). `--no-extensions` deliberately disables extension discovery so a globally installed `turn_end` handler cannot trip Pi core's boundary dispatch. The consequence is that the ContextHub `Worklog` recovery extension — which since WL-0MUQO8AEE003G1Z2 classifies `Provider finish_reason: error` as a retryable `SERVER_ERROR` and retries it — **never runs inside a driven child**. The transient reply therefore reaches Pi core, which treats a mid-stream `finish_reason: "error"` stop as a fatal turn, and the session exits 1. This is why the drive layer, not the recovery extension, must absorb it.

## Desired change

- Teach `classify_spawn_failure` a **bounded, fail-closed** `infrastructure` classification for the provider-stream signature (`Provider finish_reason: error` / `finish_reason: error`) so the existing `--infra-retry-limit` budget re-spawns the child (with the existing backoff and child comment), **or** record a documented decision (AC2b) that it must stay `unknown`, with the operator's recovery procedure. The default and expectation is option (a).
- Keep the fail-safe floor intact: a genuine child failure (non-zero exit with real work evidence, no provider signature) must still be `unknown` and hard-stop.
- Record the diagnosis and the recovery-cost measurement so the fix's value is auditable.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A written diagnosis naming the mechanism by which a `finish_reason: "error"` reply kills a driven child session (as opposed to the session retrying or degrading), evidenced from the `--no-extensions` spawner invocation and from pi and/or proxy logs.
2. Either (a) `classify_spawn_failure` learns a bounded, fail-closed `infrastructure` classification for this provider-stream signature (retried on the shared `--infra-retry-limit` budget, which must stay fail-safe for genuine defects), or (b) a documented decision records why it must stay `unknown`, with the operator's recovery procedure.
3. A test pins the new classification/decision, including the negative case that a genuine child failure (non-zero exit with real work evidence) is never retried as infrastructure.
4. The epic-driving recovery cost for a single transient reply is measured before/after (attempts needed for a 7-child epic, or an equivalent bounded harness) and recorded on this work item.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; the changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes before hand-off to review.

## Impact

A driven epic finishes without an operator babysitting dozens of manual `implement.py drive` re-runs after each flaky model reply.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo target.** The canonical source of `implement.py` is the **SorraAgents** repo at `skill/implement/` (the global install `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` is a symlink to it). This item is tracked in the ContextHub (WL) worklog; WL→SorraAgents `skill/` changes are established precedent (e.g. WL-0MWTVPL1A005KB4D). The implementer must land the change in the SorraAgents worktree and keep the placement guard satisfied.
- Do not change the Local Proxy service or the model it serves.
- Do not relax any dispatch, budget or gate behaviour. No new retry budget: the existing `--infra-retry-limit` is the bound.
- No new dependencies.
- Do not re-enable extensions in driven children (that would reintroduce the `turn_end` boundary bug the `--no-extensions` flag avoids).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — add the fail-closed `finish_reason: error` fragment to `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` (or record the decision), with a remedy string; `classify_spawn_failure` docstring/comment update.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_spawn_failure_classification.py` (new or existing spawn-classification test module) — pin the positive classification and the genuine-defect negative case.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document the new fragment, the `--no-extensions` diagnosis, and the recovery-cost measurement.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — only if the `--infra-retry-limit` help/behaviour text needs the new fragment named.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` (ContextHub, reference only) — the already-shipped retryable pattern this classification deliberately mirrors.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: `finish_reason: error` can also be a persistent misconfiguration** (unservable model, wrong key, incompatible payload) that retrying cannot fix. *Mitigation:* bounded `--infra-retry-limit` (default 5) + exponential backoff + fail-closed, non-zero-exit-with-work negative test; the remedy text names the provider so a recurrence is actionable.
- **Risk: over-broad substring matching** could reclassify a genuine test/gate failure. *Mitigation:* match the exact provider-stream signature (`Provider finish_reason: error` / `finish_reason: error`), never bare `error`; pin the negative case with realistic work evidence.
- **Risk: double retry at two layers** if extensions are ever re-enabled for driven children. *Mitigation:* document the layering (recovery extension for interactive sessions, drive classification for `--no-extensions` children).
- **Assumption:** Pi core does not internally retry a mid-stream `finish_reason: "error"`; AC1's diagnosis must evidence this (or, if it does, that the retries were exhausted).
- **Assumption:** cross-repo WL→SorraAgents `skill/` changes remain supported by the dispatcher/implement workflow.
- **Scope-creep risk:** fixing Pi core's `--extensions`/`turn_end` boundary bug or changing the proxy is out of scope. Any such discovery is recorded as a new linked work item, not absorbed here.

## Out of scope

- Changing the Local Proxy service or the model it serves.
- Relaxing any dispatch, budget or gate behaviour.
- Fixing the Pi-core `turn_end` boundary bug (the reason `--no-extensions` exists).

## Related work

- **WL-0MUQO8AEE003G1Z2** (completed) — Retry proxy `finish_reason error` in recovery: the recovery-extension retry that this item complements and explains (disabled in driven children by `--no-extensions`).
- **WL-0MUVYA3VW008CH6I**, **WL-0MUVXR39A0081774** (completed) — children of the above that shipped the retryable pattern and its test.
- **SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY** (open) — "Epic drive cannot spawn headless child sessions — pi -p fails model resolution": the adjacent spawn-failure classification path.
- **SA-0MWGZ86MS005OE61** (completed) — "implement.py drive: spawn-failed child trips the worktree-placement guard on unrelated dirt": the placement guard a re-spawned child must keep satisfying.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was repo-evidence-driven rather than interview-driven: every question below was resolved from repository inspection, so no producer input was required. Recorded for auditability (idempotent — do not duplicate on re-run).

- **Q: Which layer should absorb the transient `finish_reason: error` — the pi recovery extension or the drive loop?**
  — Answer (repo evidence): the **drive loop**. `_default_session_spawner` runs children with `--no-extensions`, which disables the ContextHub `Worklog` recovery extension (the layer WL-0MUQO8AEE003G1Z2 fixed). Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_default_session_spawner`) and `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`.
- **Q: Is the recovery extension already handling this reason, making the drive change redundant?**
  — Answer (repo evidence): No. `error-patterns.ts` classifies it as a retryable `SERVER_ERROR`, but that code is not loaded in a `--no-extensions` child. Source: `error-classification.test.ts` (classification) vs the spawner's `--no-extensions` flag.
- **Q: Which repo holds the code, and is cross-repo tracking supported?**
  — Answer (repo evidence): **SorraAgents** (`skill/implement/`; `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` is a symlink to it). Cross-repo WL→SorraAgents `skill/` work is precedent (WL-0MWTVPL1A005KB4D). Source: filesystem inode comparison and the WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD provenance table.
- **Q: Does the repo already have a spawn-classification test to extend?**
  — Answer (repo evidence): No dedicated `classify_spawn_failure` test exists; `test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` exercises spawn-failure evidence only. The implementer should add a focused classification test. Source: `rg classify_spawn_failure skill/implement/tests/`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MUVXR39A0081774** – Test: classify Provider finish_reason error as retryable (completed)
- **WL-0MUVYA3VW008CH6I** – Implement: add retryable pattern to error-patterns.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MUVY29WI0003AXG** – Test: recovery-loop retries Provider finish_reason error (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mwtad1km0081uud, 0mwtvpl1a005kb4d, abandon, abort, absorb (+314 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: abandon, abort, absorb, absorbed, ac1 (+303 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: abandon, abort, actionable, add, agent (+263 more)

# Implement: add finish_reason error to SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS

**Goal:** Teach `classify_spawn_failure` to recognise the provider-stream signature `Provider finish_reason: error` as a bounded, fail-closed `infrastructure` classification so the existing `--infra-retry-limit` budget re-spawns the child with exponential backoff.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either (a) `classify_spawn_failure` learns a bounded, fail-closed `infrastructure` classification for this provider-stream signature (retried on the shared `--infra-retry-limit` budget, which must stay fail-safe for genuine defects), or (b) a documented decision records why it must stay `unknown`, with the operator's recovery procedure. **Option (a) is the expected implementation.**
- `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` includes a tuple entry for `"finish_reason: error"` with a remedy string that names the provider and directs the operator to re-run `implement.py drive`
- The fragment matches case-insensitively (e.g. `"Provider finish_reason: error"`, `"FINISH_REASON: ERROR"`)
- A genuine child failure (non-zero exit with real work evidence, no provider signature) is never reclassified as infrastructure — it stays `unknown`
- The existing two `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` entries are unchanged
- No new dependencies are added

## Dependencies

None — this is the core implementation change that the tests in WL-0MWU78JZV002OJH4 and WL-0MWU7ADKL003HONG will verify.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — add `"finish_reason: error"` to `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` with a remedy string; update `classify_spawn_failure` docstring
- `skill/implement/tests/test_spawn_failure_classification.py` — tests that exercise the new classification

## Constraints

- The fix must be bounded: the existing `--infra-retry-limit` (default 5) + exponential backoff is the bound; do not introduce a new retry budget
- The fix must be fail-closed: a genuine child defect must stay `unknown` and hard-stop
- The remedy text must be actionable — name the provider and the recovery step

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: `finish_reason: error` can also indicate a persistent misconfiguration. Mitigation: bounded retries + fail-closed negative test; remedy names the provider.
- Assumption: cross-repo WL→SorraAgents `skill/` changes remain supported.

- A test exists under `skill/shared/tests/` (or an appropriate skill test directory) that exercises the routine-vs-handoff behaviour.

- The test follows the project's test-writing guidelines (`skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`) and passes via the canonical test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope).

## Resolved implementation choice (routine assumption — no producer review needed)

The routine-vs-handoff decision is agent judgement expressed in skill prose, so there is no runtime function to unit-test directly. The chosen approach (recorded here per the rule this item establishes, rather than parking on producer review):

- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — test-writing conventions to follow.
